It also states that the standard Positional Encoding (PE) frequency bandwidth ranges from 20 to 22 (Source [S1] notes: 'Positional Encoding (PE) frequency bandwidth ranges from 20 to 22 in standard configuration'). Furthermore, the ablation study (Figure 8 and surrounding text) demonstrates that with a small MLP (W=32), the model is insufficient, but with sufficient capacity (implied by the comparison and the standard W=256 setup), higher PE frequencies (up to 216 in ablation) help recover details. The claim that increasing PE bandwidth provides little benefit if capacity is not large is supported by the observation that a small renderer (W=32) fails to translate grid features accurately, implying that higher PE frequencies require sufficient model capacity (like W=256) to be effective, whereas without it, the benefit is limited or the model fails to utilize the high-frequency information effectively.
